title: A Study to Assess Adverse Events and How Pivekimab Sunirine Moves Through the Body of Pediatric Patients with Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
official: A Phase 1b Study of the Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Pivekimab Sunirine in Pediatric Subjects with Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
summary: Main objective: To determine the safety and pharmacokinetic profile of PVEK in pediatric subjects with relapsed/refractory CD-123-positive AML
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia;  Acute Myeloid Leukemia
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants must have histologically confirmed AML meeting one of the following disease criteria:• Second or greater relapse OR • Disease refractory to second or subsequent line of therapy (defined as resistant disease after at least one cycle of each treatment regimen)
2. Participants must have myeloid leukemic blasts that are CD123-positive by flow cytometry as determined by the treating institution.
3. Participant has ≥5% myeloid leukemic blasts in bone marrow at time of relapse or refractory disease and prior to Screening for this study.
4. Performance status by Lansky (< 16 years old at evaluation) or Karnofsky (≥ 16 years old at evaluation) score ≥ 50 or ECOG score ≤ 2.
5. Participants may have status of CNS1, CNS2, or CNS3 disease without clinical signs or neurologic symptoms suggestive of CNS leukemia, such as facial nerve palsy, brain/eye involvement or hypothalamic syndrome. Participants may have non-CNS extramedullary disease.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participant has known clinically significant cardiac disease.
2. Participant with Down syndrome
3. Participant has acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) or juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML)
4. Participant has symptomatic central nervous system (CNS3) disease
5. Participant has prior history of any severity VOD/SOS (veno-occlusive disease/sinusoidal obstructive syndrome) of the liver.
6. Participants who have received prior CAR-T therapy
